games.2026_02_DET_BUF: Buffalo enters as the third-highest-rated team after its win in Houston, and Detroit's rating slipped after needing overtime to beat New Orleans at home. The Lions' problem on a short week is the offensive line: left guard Christian Mahogany and rookie right tackle Blake Miller were ruled out Wednesday, center Juice Scruggs is questionable, and Cade Mays is already on IR, so three starting linemen are missing. Buffalo's James Cook practiced in full and is expected to play. It is the first regular-season game at the new Highmark Stadium, and model and market agree on Bills by about four and a half.
games.2026_02_CAR_ATL: Two depleted rosters and a coin flip. Atlanta lost Da'Shawn Hand for the season, still has Jalon Walker on IR and James Pearce Jr. suspended, Drake London is questionable with a shoulder, All-Pro guard Chris Lindstrom is in concussion protocol, and Stefanski still would not name a quarterback Wednesday: Cooper Rush practiced in full and is the likely starter, Tua did not practice, and Penix says he is not all the way back. Carolina is worse off on the line, with both starting tackles out at least through Week 4 and Nic Scourton done for the year, and the defense just allowed 59 points. The model has the Falcons by three at home; the market moved to Carolina by 2.5 during the week, and the blend is a dead heat.
games.2026_02_CIN_HOU: Houston rated well above Cincinnati entering the season, but the injuries are one-sided. The Texans have Braden Smith and Jayden Higgins on IR and lost two more linebackers, Henry To'oTo'o and Jake Hummel, in Week 1 with E.J. Speed already out. Cincinnati is the healthiest team on the slate and gets the full Joe Burrow adjustment, the largest quarterback boost in the model, after a 1-8 record without him last year. The roof will be closed. Model and market both make Houston a three-point favorite.
games.2026_02_CLE_TB: Tampa Bay rated five and a half points better than Cleveland before the season and the gap widened after the Browns' 34-10 loss in Jacksonville. Todd Monken kept Deshaun Watson as the starter despite a poor debut. Both teams are relatively healthy for this one, so the number is about ratings and weather: 89 degrees with a 70 percent thunderstorm chance compresses the margin slightly. The model has the Bucs by six, the market by 8.5, and the blend by about seven.
games.2026_02_GB_NYJ: Green Bay's rating fell more than a point after the loss in Minnesota and the Packers are still without Micah Parsons and Josh Jacobs, with two starting linemen questionable. But the Jets are worse off: their rating is the lowest on the slate, Minkah Fitzpatrick (groin, two to three weeks) and first-round receiver Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle, week to week) are both out, and Joseph Ossai is out. The model makes Green Bay a six-point road favorite; the market shortened to 3.5 during the week.
games.2026_02_MIN_CHI: The biggest model-versus-market gap of the week. Chicago's rating rose after the 59-point outburst in Carolina, but the Bears have Ozzy Trapilo and Tyrique Stevenson questionable and three defenders on PUP, a 2.5-point injury hit. Minnesota's quarterback is a genuine coin flip: Kyler Murray was limited Wednesday and starts if he clears concussion protocol, otherwise Carson Wentz, and the model splits the difference. The Vikings also lost running back Jordan Mason to IR with a broken thumb. The data alone has this near a pick; the market moved from Chicago by 5.5 to 4.5, and the blend settles on Bears by about two and a half.
games.2026_02_NO_BAL: Baltimore's 41-23 win in Indianapolis was the best opponent-adjusted performance of Week 1 and lifted the Ravens to fourth in the ratings. New Orleans is missing Cameron Jordan, lost rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson to IR, and Alvin Kamara was limited Wednesday in his first practice back from the MCL sprain, so he is a true game-time question. Zay Flowers did not practice Wednesday and is day to day. Model and market agree on Ravens by eight and a half to nine.
games.2026_02_PHI_TEN: Philadelphia's rating fell after the narrow win over Washington, the Eagles lost Landon Dickerson to IR, Cooper DeJean was held out of pads Wednesday, and Jonathan Greenard is still questionable. Tennessee's rating dropped too after the loss to the Jets. The model has the Eagles by under five on the road, the market by seven; the blend is six, which keeps Philadelphia a Moderate pick rather than a High one.
games.2026_02_PIT_NE: New England's rating takes the biggest injury hit on the slate: A.J. Brown went on IR with a high-ankle sprain, Harold Landry is on PUP, and TreVeyon Henderson is back at practice but not yet cleared. Pittsburgh came out of Week 1 healthy apart from DeShon Elliott on IR, and Joey Porter Jr. is ramping toward a full practice. The model still likes the Patriots at home by nearly four, but the market's 5.5 looks generous, and the blend is 4.7.
games.2026_02_JAX_DEN: The one game where the data and the market pick different teams. Jacksonville's rout of Cleveland made it the second-highest-rated team in the league, and Denver's 31-10 loss in Kansas City, with Jonathon Cooper still on the exempt list, dropped the Broncos below average. Denver also listed running back RJ Harvey and receiver Marvin Mims as non-participants Wednesday. On the data alone the Jaguars are five-and-a-half-point road favorites; the market has Denver by 2.5. The blend gives Jacksonville the narrowest of edges, so this is a coin flip either way.
games.2026_02_LV_LAC: The Chargers rated as a slight favorite before the season, but the offensive line is without Tyler Biadasz, Denzel Perryman is on IR, and Ladd McConkey did not practice Wednesday with the rib injury. Las Vegas gets the Kirk Cousins upgrade over last year's quarterback play, but center Jackson Powers-Johnson has been ruled out and Brock Bowers missed practice after his meniscus trim. The model has Los Angeles by two and a half; the market moved to 6.5, and the blend is about five.
games.2026_02_MIA_SF: The largest gap on the slate. San Francisco came out of Melbourne healthy, with Kittle, Bosa and McCaffrey all playing, and its rating rose three points on the 27-7 win. One aggregator claimed McCaffrey was placed on IR this week; no reputable outlet corroborates it and he is treated as active, so check Friday's report. Miami is a bottom-three team by rating with a first-year starter at quarterback and Kenneth Grant on IR. The model has the 49ers by twelve, the market by 13.5, and the simulation gives Miami roughly one chance in six.
games.2026_02_SEA_ARI: Seattle is the top-rated team in the model but Sam Darnold has been officially ruled out with a glute strain (no surgery, possibly back in Week 3). Drew Lock, who finished the comeback against New England, costs the Seahawks about two and a half points, and Nick Emmanwori remains questionable. Arizona is short James Conner and has two starters questionable, but its rating jumped after the upset in Los Angeles. Roof closed. The model has Seattle by five and a half; the market shortened from 4.5 to 3.5 once Darnold was ruled out.
games.2026_02_WAS_DAL: Two below-average teams getting worse. Dallas lost Tyler Smith to IR, Malik Hooker is doubtful after forearm surgery, and DeMarvion Overshown is questionable; Washington is still without Laremy Tunsil, Johnny Newton and Trey Amos, and Frankie Luvu and Chig Okonkwo are questionable after Week 1 exits. Jayden Daniels grades as a modest upgrade on last year's Commanders quarterback play. Roof closed. The market moved to Cowboys by 4.5 during the week; the model has three, and the blend is about three and a half.
games.2026_02_IND_KC: Kansas City's rating climbed after the Monday-night win and Mahomes came through his return healthy, but Josh Simmons and Chamarri Conner did not practice Wednesday and are now doubtful. Indianapolis dropped more than three points after being routed at home by Baltimore. The weather is the wild card: a 70 percent rain chance and 15 mph wind at Arrowhead pull the margin and the total down. The model has the Chiefs by five and a half, the market by 6.5.
games.2026_02_NYG_LA: The Rams fell three points in the ratings after the loss in Melbourne and then lost Myles Garrett to IR until at least Week 6. Aaron Donald's roster exemption has been lifted and a Monday-night debut is described as very realistic, while Puka Nacua is being taken day by day. New York's Jaxson Dart played well in Dallas and Malik Nabers is back. Los Angeles gets extra rest after its Thursday game in Australia. The model has the Rams by five, the market by seven, and the blend by six.
